The liver weight increases induced in mice by the steroidal aglycone alkaloids solanidine, solasonine, tomatidine and dehydroepiandrostenedione were greater than the increases induced by the glycoalkaloi ds alpha-chaconne, alpha-solanine and alpha-tomatine.
the potato glyco-alkaloids, alpha-chaconin and alpha-solanin, are nontoxic to the liver, but that the aglycone solanidine is hepatotoxic and that this toxicity is reversible.
the liver weights of mice fed diets containing the steroidal glyco- or aglycones of potato, tomato or eggplant were affected by the type of compound, the dose and the time of feeding.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and quantification of the effects of naturally occurring steroidal alkaloids and aglycones on food consumption and body weight, and the determination of the potential toxicity of these compounds in mice.
the identification of the most toxic steroidal glyco- and aglycones in plant foods.
the potential toxicity of plant steroidal alkaloids and aglycones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steroidal aglycone solanidine is more toxic than the glycoalkaloidal precursor alpha-chaconin in mice and the steroidal agylcone solasodine has a similar toxicity.
potato, tomato and solasonine glycoalkaloidal consumption does not appear to be toxic in mice.
the aglycon of the potato glyco-alkaloids, solanidine, is the toxic component in potato tubers and that solanidine and the aglycon, solasodines of eggplant are toxic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aglycone form of a steroidal glyco-alkaloid is more toxic than its glyco-alkylated parent compound.
potato glycoalkaoids are relatively non-toxic to mice and are less toxic than the corresponding aglycones and DHEA.

the most toxic glycoalkaloidal compounds, alpha-chaconin and alpha-solanin, were removed from the plant by boiling and that the most toxic aglycones, solanidine and DHEA, were removed by cooking in the presence of water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver weights of mice are affected by dietary steroidal glyco- and aglycones.
the aglycon form of the steroidal glyco-alkaloids is more toxic than the glyco-alkaoid form.
the liver is a good target organ for evaluating the toxicity of steroidal alkaloids and that the effects of these compounds are structure dependent.
